question: Does Envoy generic differ from AGW generic on ISL4000 when successful requests are counted over identical-length, fully overlapping six-client measurement windows?
intent: paired gateway-host diagnosis; the former summary-only 45-second series is contextual, not a direct reference

execution.aiperf_version_resolution: Reference-reproduction exception: the paired gateway series and Claude reference pin AIPerf 0.12.0; latest stable 0.13.0 was verified on 2026-09-26, but its single-manager Mooncake preparation failed before measurement
execution.repeat_rationale: The prior summary-only ISL4000 comparison was consequential but confounded by unequal client start spread; record-level overlap resolves the timing ambiguity

measurement.primary_metric: successful request completions per second in a 30-second common interior window within each arm's six-client Job
measurement.common_window_rule: For each Job independently, t0 is the latest of its six AIPerf profile start times plus 2 seconds and t1=t0+30 seconds; require all six profile end times at least 2 seconds after t1. Count only records with request_start_ns and request_end_ns both inside [t0,t1]. The two sequential Jobs use separate absolute timestamps but identical 30-second window definitions.
measurement.request_integrity: every summary success must have exactly one well-formed profiling record and no duplicate x_request_id per Job
measurement.uncertainty: one run per arm is diagnostic; a small delta cannot support a final gateway ranking without a measured series noise floor

quality_gates: Single active gateway, six clients on pinned nodes, identical dataset/image/flags, zero request errors/cancellations, complete request records, at least 30 seconds of shared interior window
comparison_limit: Changing export level creates a new series. Request-record instrumentation may lower absolute throughput relative to summary-only results; never compare the two series as a gain or loss.
